data.narrative:
Cellcolabs is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Mattias Bernow that has raised $37M to date. The valuation landscape for early-stage biotech remains sparse; while 3 public comparables exist in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) alongside 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, few direct peer matches at the same stage and valuation tier are available for robust triangulation.

Of the three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total raised ($37M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $74M. The public-comp anchoring method—which identified a Biotech & Health P/S median of 8.1x across three tickers—cannot be deployed without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely provide. Peer-median analysis was similarly constrained by an insufficient narrow peer set meeting stage and tier filters.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, centered on $74M, derived solely from stage-progression mechanics. This range is notably narrow and rests on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, limited same-stage peer comparables, and the dependency on a 2.0x multiplier assumption. Investors should seek additional qualitative signals (IP depth, clinical progress, team) to validate this quantitative floor.
